measuredBy: Captain, re-measured after installing the D source packs and after resolving each source by content hash across every mounted root as well as by its declared path
whatThisIs: A dispatch aid. For every SOURCE_READY family it asks, per bound source, whether the path resolves to a file in a mounted custody and whether that file's first bytes are a PDF header, then compares the required components' official forms against the sources that are held PDFs.
whatThisIsNot: Not a state change, not a source determination, not a reclassification, and not a new gate. No family's state, source record, count or treatment is altered by this file, and a family listed here as unbuildable today may be perfectly buildable once its source is acquired or converted by whoever owns that decision.
whyItExists: sourceReadiness.ready reports that a source RESOLVED. PF16 was dispatched at three families that all read ready true with no reasons, and stopped on held-source facts: every Montana official form is a Word document, and four of five Illinois PRB form labels identify no document. Sending a build lane at a family in that state spends a worker to rediscover something measurable here in seconds.

whatChangedSinceTheFirstPass: The D source packs (rcap-d-source-packs-2026-08-12, three archives verified against pinned digests, 343 files) are installed and comparable; on 2026-09-08 that custody was not mounted.

A source is now resolved by content hash across the mounted roots as well as by its declared path. That is what the row gate does — it reports 'found by content hash because the declared path is in a custody that is not mounted here' and passes — so the first pass, which resolved only by declared path, understated what a builder can open.

PF16 was dispatched at three families this aid already classed unbuildable and spent a worker rediscovering it. That is the cost this record exists to prevent, and it is why the aid is kept current rather than written once.
